title: Gold Jumps 2% as Fed's Waller Cools Rate Hike Expectations
excerpt: Spot gold surged past $4,470 an ounce after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller signaled openness to holding rates steady, pulling the dollar to a one-week low.
body:
• Spot gold rose 2% to $4,472.94 per ounce on September 3, its highest since August 28, after Fed Governor Waller's dovish comments.
  • Traders scaled back September rate hike expectations to 54% from 62% following Waller's remarks.
  • The U.S. dollar dropped to a one-week low, while Treasury yields eased, both supporting bullion prices.
  • Middle East tensions and rising oil prices continue to underpin gold's safe-haven appeal ahead of Friday's nonfarm payrolls report.

Gold prices surged on Thursday after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said recent progress on inflation could justify keeping interest rates unchanged at the central bank's next meeting — a shift in tone that pulled the dollar lower and sent bullion to its strongest level in a week.

Spot gold climbed 2% to $4,472.94 per ounce by mid-morning in New York, while U.S. gold futures for December delivery rose 2.3% to $4,517.40. The rally extended a recovery that began late Wednesday after gold had fallen to its lowest level since August 7.

Waller Signals Restraint

Waller told reporters on Thursday that if upcoming data confirms inflation pressures are easing, he would argue in favor of holding rates steady at the September 15-16 Federal Open Market Committee meeting. The comment marked a notable departure from the hawkish tone set by Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh at Jackson Hole last week, where he flagged persistent inflation risks.

Markets responded swiftly. According to CME Group's FedWatch Tool, the probability of a rate hike at the September meeting fell to about 54%, down from 62% before Waller spoke. "I think traders at the moment are looking at the Fed being less aggressive with rates," said Bob Haberkorn, senior market strategist at StoneX. "More and more traders are coming around to the idea that the Fed could do one rate hike, but there probably isn't much more they can do with rates after that."

Dollar and Yields Retreat

The U.S. dollar dropped to a one-week low on Thursday, making greenback-priced bullion more affordable for overseas buyers. Treasury yields also edged lower, reducing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold.

The dollar's decline followed Wednesday's soft ADP employment report, which showed private payrolls growing less than expected in August. A sharp rally in the Japanese yen added further downward pressure on the greenback.

Middle East Tensions Add Support

Geopolitical risk continues to provide a floor for gold. Oil prices headed for a fourth consecutive day of gains, touching six-week highs after fresh U.S. airstrikes on Iranian targets and retaliatory drone and missile attacks by Tehran across the Gulf region. Rising energy prices have stoked inflation concerns, complicating the Fed's calculus.

"A rebound in oil prices after renewed U.S.-Iran tensions added to inflation concerns," said Bas Kooijman, CEO of DHF Capital. "A pricier crude could continue to tighten monetary policy expectations and drive yields higher, limiting any rebound potential for gold."

All Eyes on Friday's Jobs Report

The market's next test comes Friday with the August nonfarm payrolls report, followed by CPI and PPI inflation data next week. A softer-than-expected jobs number could reinforce the case for a Fed pause and extend gold's rally, while strong hiring data could revive rate-hike bets and pressure the metal.

Silver gained 1.7% to $66.41 per ounce, platinum rose 2% to $1,795.67, and palladium climbed 2.6% to $1,380.66.
